steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Good hustle these past few days, everybody. Let's break a bit early today—we're still twenty-five klicks out from the objective. If we make good time tomorrow morning, I think we'll get there by the afternoon.

steps.name: Field Operator A
steps.text: Thanks, Meteor. I thought we'd be gnawing on rations in the field. I didn't expect we'd get proper hot meals.

steps.name: Field Operator B
steps.text: Yeah, never knew you were such a good cook.

steps.name: Field Operator A
steps.text: So what's stewing today? It smells great, I caught a whiff of it while I was pegging the tents.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: It's a hometown specialty.

steps.name: Field Operator B
steps.text: A secret family recipe?

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Nah, I lost my parents when I was very young. It was a village household by the mountains that helped me grow. They're all good and kind people.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: This soup is something they taught me. It's simple to make, and good for cooking out in the wilds.

steps.name: Field Operator B
steps.text: Ah... sorry I brought it up.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: What's to be sorry for? It's alright.

steps.name: Field Operator B
steps.text: Oh, it smells amazing. Can I ask for the recipe?

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Of course. It's not complicated.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: You need spinach roots and wild gingerflax I just took the chance to dig up, the striped scalecis we caught this afternoon, and I used some pickled jerky and salt I brought along to season, then let it stew for fifteen minutes. Then you're good to go.

steps.name: Field Operator B
steps.text: So this is what everyone meant when they said we wouldn't regret going with you.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Hardly, I just know a few simple country dishes. I could never compare to a chef like Matterhorn.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Phew. Though, if I could, adding a pinch of staricitron seeds would've made it even better. There's a little spicy kick to them. Drinking some hot meat soup peppered with them can really brush the cold away on days like these.

steps.name: Field Operator B
steps.text: Staricitron...? It rings a bell, I've heard of a rare tree with the same name. I think it's a wood that a lot of nobles love for furniture.

steps.name: Field Operator A
steps.text: Ah, and I remember it's a species unique to Kazimierz.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: *Sigh*...

steps.name: Field Operator A
steps.text: Meteor, your home is in Kazimierz. If you've seen them before, why not tell us a little about them.

steps.name: Field Operator B
steps.text: Right, we really want to know more about where you came from.

steps.name: Field Operator A
steps.text: Meteor? Meteor, why are you so quiet?

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Hm?! Ah, my home...

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: I've been away for so long. Just what were they like...

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: It's not coming to me straight away.

steps.name: Field Operator A
steps.text: Aw, that's a shame—hey! What are you hitting me for?

steps.name: Field Operator B
steps.text: Eat up, kiddo, or you won't grow any taller.

steps.name: Field Operator A
steps.text: Do you see this, Meteor?!

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Alright, alright, it's getting late. Pour another bowl. I brought some of Matterhorn's crackers too. You can all share them.

steps.name: Field Operator A
steps.text: Wow, that's incredible! Thanks, Meteor.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Turn in as soon as you're done. I'm a little tired. I'll be going to sleep first.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Where am I? It's so dark.
Meteor, Meteor.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Who is it?
Come quick, Meteor. I've been waiting for you forever.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Who are you?
Meteor, come with me. There's going to be a moonshadow in the sky tonight. We can climb the staricitron tree and see the twin moons.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Lana? What are you doing here?
I've been waiting for you here all this time.
Listen. The wind passing through the damp leaves. It's been pushing me on.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Wind? There's no wind here, Lana. Come here, quick. Don't leave this place.
I'm going, Meteor. Quick, follow me...

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Come back, Lana! Where are you going?
Come quick, Meteor. You know I'm waiting for you.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: She's... gone.
Meteor! Meteor!

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Um... Uncle, why are you here...?

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: No, never mind. That's right, have you seen Lana? She just came by, and I don't know where she ran off to.
You're mixed up. Lana's been sick for a month now. How's she going outside?

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: She's sick?! But just now, I swear she was... this is strange... um, how is she, then? Is she any better?
*Sigh* Not much to cheer for. Barely gets her porridge down her in the morning, and she sicks up half a bowl of pink.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: How could that be! What about a doctor, then, Uncle? Has a doctor seen her?!
Meteor, it's... why I came to see you today. We've got no real options left now. This winter's gone on too long, autumn was too short. Not a thing left over.
Whole host of the village children are already beyond sickly. If we can't get any more medicine for Lana, she won't be able to make it through the winter.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: I still have a bit of savings! I'll give you all of—

...Meteor, it's not enough... there's a man who passed by and said, he wants some staricitron wood. He gets the timber, he'll leave us some money and supplies. We can pull through the winter with those.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Does he have to have those staricitron trees? Countless generations of my family's looked after that forest.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: What about other trees, will other trees do? I'm begging you. Just wait a little longer, and we might have some other way. We will...
No, Meteor, we... don't. We love them just as much as you do, but...

steps.name: Sorrowful Voice
steps.text: Help me, Meteor—*cough* *cough*—we've got no other way.

steps.name: Immature Voice
steps.text: Meteor, save me!

steps.name: Wizened Voice
steps.text: Meteor—save an old girl!

steps.name: Anxious Voice
steps.text: Meteor, Meteor!

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Ah—ahh, ahh! I'll save you all, I will—*huff* *huff*—*urk*—

steps.name: Field Operator A
steps.text: Meteor, what's wrong? It was a nightmare, wasn't it? It's okay, it's okay, we're all here.

steps.name: Field Operator B
steps.text: We are. Meteor, want some water? I'll pour you a cup.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Haagh—it's you. I thought...

steps.name: Field Operator A
steps.text: The pressure of the rescue mission probably got too much. Here, Meteor, wipe that sweat off.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: It's alright. Thank you both. My nerves must be taut, running all this way for days. I'm a little worn out.

steps.name: Field Operator B
steps.text: Meteor, if you want to tell us anything, feel free. We'll help however we can.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: It really is alright. We all still need to be on our way. Let's get our things packed and go. I'll be fine.

steps.name: Field Operator A
steps.text: Meteor!

steps.name: Field Operator B
steps.text: (Shaking head) Leave it, Keira. Don't ask.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Ah Fêng, how far are we from the objective?

steps.name: Field Operator B
steps.text: Not far now. Less than three kilometers left—

steps.name: Field Operator A
steps.text: Oh, crap. Meteor, look. In the direction of the objective.

steps.name: Field Operator B
steps.text: That's intensely thick smoke. The report didn't mention anything about a fire.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Keira, go look for survivors in the neighboring villages, and band them together to put the fire out! Ah Fêng, get the medicals ready! People have to be hurt with a fire this big! Quick!

steps.name: Field Operator A
steps.text: On it. Meteor, what about you?

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: I'll look closer to the scene, and see if I can find any other survivors!

steps.name: Field Operator A
steps.text: You be careful, then, Meteor!

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: I will! Keep yourselves safe too!

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: (The fire's burning too intensely. I can't tell if there's still anyone inside.)

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Is anyone there? If you can hear me, please answer me! Is anyone there!

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Is anyone there? If you can hear me, please answer me! Is anyone there!

steps.name: Collapsed Villager
steps.text: Is-Is that you, Meteor? Get away!

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: What's going on? Uncle, I just heard a massive explosion come from here, and I ran right over.

steps.name: Collapsed Villager
steps.text: Run, quick! Don't come near. Those tree-felling Originium engines the knight-lord brought in exploded. There's Originium dust scattered all over here.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Uncle, just save your voice for now. I'll bind the wound for you. Who else is here?

steps.name: Collapsed Villager
steps.text: No, no, you listen to me, Meteor. Get away, quick. You don't go, you won't make it. Those machines might explode again at any time. You... you'll catch ill! Quick, get away from here!

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Uncle, I—I can't leave you all behind. Hang in there. I'll bring you out now.

steps.name: Wounded Villager
steps.text: Argh! My eyes—it hurts!

steps.name: Howling Villager
steps.text: My leg! My leg's gone! Urgh—save me, save my soul!

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: (What do I do, what do I do, what do I do? Dammit, what should I be doing?!)

steps.name: Collapsed Villager
steps.text: What are you still gazing off for? Get out of here. It's dangerous!

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Huh—?

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: *cough* *cough* *cough*—my throat... ghaagh—*cough* *cough* *cough*...

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: (The back of my hand's... bloody. Did I cut it?)

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Uncle! Uncle, are you still alright? Un... cle... are you all...

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Answer me! Agh—*cough* *cough*—answer me... *urk*.

steps.name: Collapsed Villager
steps.text: Me... teor... come here...

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Oh, Uncle! Go on, I'm listening!

steps.name: Collapsed Villager
steps.text: We're—*cough* *cough*... all so sorry for you... but Lana... she asked you...

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Uncle! Uncle!

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: How could this happen?

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: How is everything I do wrong? How is everything I do useless...?

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: How...
By all rights, her face should be scorched dry by the blistering air, yet Meteor feels wet droplets, rolling down.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: (Rubs back of hand against cheek)

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Ugh—dammit, I can't believe I'm remembering that at a time like this.
Ohhhh, my child...

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: (What's that noise? Is there someone crying?)

steps.name: Mournful Woman
steps.text: Ohhh, my child! You wretch, why save me? You should've left me to die, how could you not save our child?!

steps.name: Anguished Man
steps.text: Darling, it's my fault, I couldn't save our girl... ohh, my precious baby, Daddy's so sorry... *sobbing*

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Why are you still here? Get out of here, quick!

steps.name: Mournful Woman
steps.text: Go? How? We can't go a step more. Our whole lives are ruined here... ohhh...

steps.name: Anguished Man
steps.text: Miss. My leg's hurt. I can't walk. Get my wife out of here, forget about me. Quick, move!

steps.name: Mournful Woman
steps.text: I'm not going—*sobbing*—We're together as a family, and we'll die as a family. Ohhh, my child.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: What's happening? Is there still someone inside?

steps.name: Anguished Man
steps.text: Yes—*sobbing*—my girl's still in there. We were in a rush, and I—I was only in time to rescue my wife, and I left—the disgrace I am, I left my child in there... *sobbing*

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Okay, sir. Save your breath. Do you still remember which part of the house your child was in?

steps.name: Anguished Man
steps.text: You won't be time—the fire's too big. Get my wife out of here. It's all hopeless.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: (Grasps the man's collar) Where is she?!

steps.name: Anguished Man
steps.text: In her bedroom—s—southmost part of the attic.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Got it. Look after your lady.

steps.name: Anguished Man
steps.text: Watch out—

steps.name: Mournful Woman
steps.text: *cough* *cough*...

steps.name: Anguished Man
steps.text: Darling? Darling, what's wrong? Someone, anyone! Save her!

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: (It's all burning too fast. My eyes hurt so much.)

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Little girl, can you hear me? *cough* *cough* *cough*....

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: (South of the attic... oh, there!)

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Agh, hot—*cough* *cough*.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: (Can only kick it open.)

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: (I can't see anything clear. Dammit, all this thick smoke.)

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Is anyone there? *cough* *cough*—
Save... help me...

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: (That voice came from the wardrobe!)

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: I've found you. Oh, thank goodness.

steps.name: Semiconscious Girl
steps.text: Daddy... mo...

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: She's losing consciousness already. Hold on, I'll take you away from here.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: (Lifts up the girl)
Only when Meteor looks back does she realize the way she came has now been engulfed by the inferno.

The scarlet blaze trails along the walls, stairs and doorframe as it spreads, the searing licks roiling and twisting without end, attempting to charge for the two in the room, lapping at their clothes and skin.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: (Agh, now what do I do?!)

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Dammit—it's collapsing!

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: *cough* *cough* *cough*—*hiss*, *huff*—

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: (I think my back got struck. It hurts. Right, the child!)

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: (Phew... wonderful, she's alright. No, I need to think of a way to get out fast, I need to get up.)

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Argh, it really does hurt.

steps.name: Semiconscious Girl
steps.text: H-Help... me...

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: I'll help you, I'll help you, I absolutely will.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: (Looks all around)

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: (There's a gap there. I think I can climb through. It should be from when the wall fell in the collapse just now.)

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: (This hole is too small, I can't make it in. I can only get the child through first.)

steps.name: Field Operator A
steps.text: Meteor, are you there?! *cough* *cough* *cough* Where are you?

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Keira!!

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Is that Keira?! I'm in here, I'm in here! South, there's a small hole here!

steps.name: Field Operator A
steps.text: Meteor! Ah, I see you! How'll we get through a hole this small? What now? *whimper*

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Don't cry, don't mind me for now. The child, get the child away!

steps.name: Field Operator A
steps.text: Meteor!

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Grab onto the child, careful of any splinters.

steps.name: Field Operator A
steps.text: What about you then, Meteor?! I'll go find Fêng, you wait for me, hold on—

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Listen, forget about me, you won't make it. Get the child away quick. Go.

steps.name: Field Operator A
steps.text: Meteor, no, I can't do that, I'll find some way. We can definitely make it back together. Eargh—

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Eek—no, it's too heavy, Keira, we can't push it apart!

steps.name: Field Operator A
steps.text: We'll try again! Hold onto my hand, and don't let go, Meteor!

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Quickly, go! Or else you'll be in danger too!

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Damn it all, get the child out of here!!

steps.name: Field Operator A
steps.text: Meteor!!!!

steps.name: Lana
steps.text: Meteor...

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Lana... I've been waiting for so long...

steps.name: Lana
steps.text: (Shakes head)

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: I'm sorry.

steps.name: Lana
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: I couldn't save you, and I couldn't save everyone. In the end... I couldn't protect a single thing...

steps.name: Lana
steps.text: No, you've already done so well. It's enough, now... it's enough.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Were you waiting for me to go with you?

steps.name: Lana
steps.text: No. I came to say goodbye.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Goodbye?

steps.name: Lana
steps.text: (Hugging) I'm leaving, Meteor. Don't come with me.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: You're going, in the end?

steps.name: Lana
steps.text: Yes. Don't cry. You're the bravest little hunter. You've still got such a long road to walk, and still so many people who need you.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: I miss you, so much. I really do.

steps.name: Lana
steps.text: I miss you too, but it's time now. Go on, let me go.

steps.name: Lana
steps.text: See you...

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Meteor, you're awake. How do you feel?

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Mi...

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Making it out alive with injuries as serious as that, it's nothing short of a miracle.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: You'd better not pull this next time, heading on missions without any regard for your own safety. Both me and Gianna were worried sick about you.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Pfffheh.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Agh! That hurts.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: What are you laughing about?! You've got burns all over your back, your windpipe's burnt, you have a fracture in your spinal column... do you want me to keep tallying for you?

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: I thought... you'd be crying your... eyes out over me—*cough* *cough*!

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: What, is that the kind of person I am to you?

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Oof... *huff*. Sorry, Mina, for causing you and all of the Medical such hassle.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: What are you being guilty for? We're just doing our jobs.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Hfff—Well, I'm sorry, but I'm powerless to promise you that.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: You—

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Medical gave everything they had to pull you from the cold hands of death this time, but IF there's a next time, we'll all be powerless to promise anything.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: I... couldn't just look on as it all happened. I... don't ever want to see people stuck in those circumstances again, truly.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Between a rock and a hard place.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Not one person should ever be forced to make such a choice, forced to part, forced through... loss.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: I can't do it, it's just... I can't.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Meteor, are you still brooding on the past?

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: I knew it, I can't hide anything from you.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: At the time, I believed if I just sacrificed the forest I always protected, I'd get to have Lana back, have everyone in the village living peacefully again.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: But fate really was too voracious. What it wanted wasn't just my concession.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: I gave it an inch, and it wanted a mile, until it stripped my pockets bare of anything left.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: We've chatted about this before. Holding onto the past without letting go doesn't solve anything.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: You're right. And it's not like I don't understand.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: After Lana passed from illness, I took up her bow, and left the forest together with the other Oripathy sufferers.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: In those days wandering, I spent ages in a muddle. I hated that noble who refused to shoulder any blame, and left with nothing but a pat on the buttocks.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: And I hated myself, powerless to protect my loved ones, the things I cherished.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: But when I first met you, you were nothing like that. What happened?

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: I suppose I saw more, and my outlook changed.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: The people who once went with me walked, scattered, and I was left alone aimlessly drifting.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: I only gradually came to realize, there's so many people across this land who've been through the same things I have, who all struggled painfully through such desperate dilemmas.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Having personally experienced that stress, how could I just stand and watch as others go through the same torture? That's why I'm willing and ready, regardless of the danger.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Because those smiles, lost then found again, make me feel like my heart is filled full once more.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Fine.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: Seeing as... this is how you think, I don't have much more I can say. While you've been unconscious these past few days, Gianna's been watching your bedside the whole time. You remember to give her a proper thanks.

steps.name: Medic Operator
steps.text: I've got matters to attend to, so I'll be heading off now. Rest up well.

steps.name: Field Operator A
steps.text: Gianna, Meteor just woke up. When we see her in a moment, make sure you don't throw yourself on her.

steps.name: Gianna
steps.text: I know, Keira. I folded Meteor a whole vase of roses, and on every single one I wrote a well wishing thing. If she has this, she'll get better real soon.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: (Smiles and shakes head) This little rascal.

steps.name: Field Operator A
steps.text: Meteor, I heard from Mina you were awake. How are you?

steps.name: Gianna
steps.text: Meteor, you... you... waaahh—you're finally awake! I was so scared!

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: Gianna, don't cry. I'll be all better before you know it.

steps.name: Gianna
steps.text: ...Um, this vase is for you.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: What's this?

steps.name: Field Operator A
steps.text: Don't ask, Gianna spent ages folding it. While you were out, Mina caught the little mite awake at night over and over, just folding roses.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: I'm sorry, Gianna, for making you worry.

steps.name: Gianna
steps.text: I don't want you to be sorry. Can you promise me you won't get hurt anymore? I get really scared I won't see you again.

steps.name: Meteor
steps.text: I won't, Gianna, I won't.

steps.name: Gianna
steps.text: Waaahhhh, Meteooor!!!

steps.name: Field Operator A
steps.text: Gianna, stop crying!
